title: What Will We Miss?
beats: Year 6009 reads the same upside down; you will not live to see it
Framing question: what future events will we miss? Time pyramid, 1 block per 10 years, done in 3183
Chernobyl zone safe around 22000; supernovas of Betelgeuse in under a million years
Supernova brighter than the full Moon, a second sun in daytime
Milky Way named for milk; stars as drops of milk, Andromeda the blur
Andromeda approaching at 300 km/s; sky now vs in 2 billion vs 3.75 billion years
Simulation runs billions of years per second; in a human life it looks frozen
Don't FOMO: future people will envy us (the beginning of the Internet)
Future losses: total eclipses (600 My), Niagara (52000), Rushmore (7 My), Saturn's rings
Sums up the list of what the future will not have
Flip to what you missed: your conception and birth; whenwasiconceived.com tool
Online calculator returns week, #1 song and movie of that week
Photon random walk out of a star compared to gestation, then birth
Find a star as many light years away as you are old; its light left when you were born
Space is so big you don't have to miss everything; sign-off

metrics.examples: ~10 timed events, roughly ascending from 6009 years to 3.75 billion, then a descending turn to your own life
metrics.ending: Personal payoff: the light from a star your age away; reframes the 'missing out' hook

principles.1: confirmed: begins from upside-down year numerals, concrete pyramid and a Milky Way name, ends in your birth
principles.2: confirmed: only new interface is one web tool at 7:20
principles.4: confirmed: milk etymology to galaxy; gestation to photon escape; stepchild to Milkdromeda
principles.5: partly: sky shown as you would see it now vs in 2 and 3.75 billion years (3:15)
principles.7: partly: the list pattern of 'you will miss X' repeats so viewer anticipates; the insight is stated, not found
principles.8: partly: speech steady; novelty is paced by a list of short items and a single longer simulation beat 3:15-4:36
principles.9: confirmed: the 'will miss' list structure repeats ~10 times
principles.10: partly: scales grow from 6009 years to billions, not strictly tiny-to-big (Chernobyl and supernova jumps)
principles.11: partly: Milky Way and milk explained before Andromeda; otherwise a list
principles.12: confirmed: Chernobyl, time pyramid, calculator website, Niagara, granite erosion rate
principles.13: partly: playful accessible tone, little 'why this tool' reasoning

new_moves.name: scale-ladder-list
new_moves.what: A run of events at escalating timescales sharing one frame ('missing out')

new_moves.name: flip-the-frame-to-you
new_moves.what: After cosmic scales, pivots to the viewer's own life to land emotionally

new_moves.name: personalised-tool
new_moves.what: Uses an interactive calculator so the abstract fact becomes the viewer's own number

theory: The video is a single repeated frame (what you will miss) hung on a ladder of timescales, then folded back onto the viewer so deep time becomes personal. A list structure plus a closing personalised fact does the teaching, not derivation.
velocity: Scene builder: timescale-ladder scene with log-scale ruler and the learner's own age as a marker
Orchestrator: end abstract topics by binding a quantity to the learner's own data (birthday, location)
Voice: use callback to the opening hook in the final beat
Learner model: track which scale examples landed; reuse the best as anchor
quote: space is so gosh darn big you don't have to miss out on everything
